# ethereum-optimism/optimism Weekly Report (Jun 14 - 20, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week, the Optimism ecosystem focused on modernizing its testing infrastructure and advancing the Permissionless Codepath (PCD) deployment pipeline. A major refactoring of the `op-e2e` suite transitioned the default L2 Execution Layer to `op-reth`, resolving critical compatibility issues with deprecated block sealing mechanisms. Significant progress was also made in the Rust stack, centralizing hardfork mappings and improving the stability of `op-reth` through upstream bug fixes and enhanced transaction reproduction logic.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### `op-e2e` Testing & Infrastructure Modernization
The testing framework underwent a substantial update to ensure compatibility with newer block sealing mechanisms, specifically for Karst/Osaka blocks.
*   **Transition to `op-reth`:** Refactored the `op-e2e` suite to default to `op-reth` for L2 Execution Layer operations, addressing hangs in interop super-cannon tests caused by the deprecation of `op-geth` ([#21363](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21363)).
*   **Superchain Registry Integration:** Introduced features to build OP Mainnet and Sepolia chainspecs directly from the superchain registry, reducing reliance on hardcoded configurations ([#21374](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21374), [#21397](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21397)).

### Rust Stack & `op-reth` Stability
Development focused on aligning the Rust implementation with protocol requirements and improving node reliability.
*   **Hardfork Management:** Centralized the mapping of OP forks to their implied L1 forks (e.g., Karst to Osaka) to ensure consistency across the stack ([#21368](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21368), [#21384](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21384)).
*   **Transaction Reproduction:** Fixed a bug in `op-reth` regarding the reproduction of trailing SDM PostExec transactions during block rebuilding to maintain consensus ([#21321](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21321)).
*   **Upstream Fixes:** Resolved a SIGBUS crash and infinite retry loop in `op-reth` proofs-history via upstream updates ([#20934](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20934)).

### Smart Contracts & Chain Operations
Refinements were made to genesis state generation and interop testing tools.
*   **Genesis Fixes:** Addressed a critical issue by clearing residual proxy admin owner nonces in L2 genesis, preventing unintended nonce increments during implementation updates ([#21343](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21343)).
*   **Interop Tooling:** Added new testing tools for interop bridges, including `check-lagoon` and `interop-smoke` ([#21395](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21395)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Protocol Consistency:** Successfully resolved the latent bug in Karst-to-Osaka mapping and finalized the centralization of fork mappings ([#21338](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21338)).
*   **Stale Issue Cleanup:** A significant number of legacy issues (over 15) related to dispute monitoring, Ledger UX, and old test tasks were closed as superseded or stale, streamlining the project's backlog.

### New & Active Issues
*   **Permissionless Codepath (PCD) Milestone 4:** Several new issues outline the requirements for the permissionless deployment pipeline, including the need for artifact persistence across workflow phases ([#21376](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21376)) and a new `netchef` workflow to support both permissioned and permissionless network creation ([#21375](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21375)).
*   **Withdrawal Mechanisms:** A new initiative was launched to implement one-day permissioned withdrawals, involving contract changes and on-chain constants ([#21390](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21390)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week saw active maintenance of external dependencies, with several Dependabot PRs updating core libraries like `otel`, `crypto`, and `websocket`. Documentation efforts were prominent, including the release of a runbook for recovering interop networks from invalid-message reorgs ([#21391](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21391)) and updated release notes for `proxyd v4.28.1`. Collaboration between the protocol and dev-ops teams is evident in the coordinated push toward the Milestone 4 Permissionless Codepath.
